question.text: For air at room temperature, the atmospheric pressure is $1.0 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$ and density of ait is $1.2 \mathrm{kgm}^{-3}$. For a tube of length $1.0 \mathrm{m}$, closed at one end, the lowest frequency $\begin{array}{lllllll}\text { generated is } & 84 & \text { Hz. } & \text { The } & \text { value } & \text { of } \boldsymbol{\gamma}\end{array}$ (ratio of two specific heats) for air is

solution.text: The tube is closed at one end. So, it will act like a closed organ pipe. The lowest frequency produced in the tube $$ \begin{array}{l} l=\frac{\lambda}{4}, \lambda=4 \\ l=1 \mathrm{m} \\ f=84 \mathrm{Hz} \\ V=n \lambda=84 \times 4 \end{array} $$ When wave propagate in air, the velocity Here, $$ \begin{array}{l} v=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma p}{\rho}} \\ p=1.0 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{array} $$ $$ \begin{aligned} \rho &=1.2 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ V^{2} &=\frac{\gamma P}{\rho} \\ \gamma &=\frac{\mathrm{v}^{2} \cdot \rho}{\mathrm{P}} \\ &=\frac{(84 \times 4)^{2} \times 1.2}{1.0 \times 10^{5}} \\ &=\frac{135472.2}{10^{5}}=1.354 \\ &=1.4 \end{aligned} $$
